statement: Conflict is distinct from indeterminacy.
Conflict does not imply partial effect.
Partial effect does not imply conflict.
Conflict does not imply fork.
Resolved conflict remains historically evidenced.
Fork is a structured divergence in recognized state or history.
Fork does not imply invalidity.
Canonicality requires an explicit governing rule.
Canonical branch selection does not erase noncanonical history.
Observation does not imply occurrence.
Observation conflict does not imply effect conflict.
Stale does not mean false.
Reconciliation does not itself mutate financial state.
Reconciliation does not create repair authority.
Consensus does not imply reconciliation.
Majority observation does not imply reconciliation.
Reconciled does not imply restored.
Reconciled does not imply settlement finality.
Reconciled does not imply continuity preservation.
Economic branch convergence does not imply historical identity.
Conflict != Fork != Reconciliation != Restoration != Finality != ContinuityPreserved.
